new_entities.name: School social-emotional learning
new_entities.description: Universal or classroom-delivered social-emotional learning programs in schools.

new_entities.name: Child mental health outcomes
new_entities.description: Broad child and adolescent mental health outcomes including emotional symptoms, behavior, prosociality, and related wellbeing measures.

edges.effect_quant: A 2011 meta-analysis of 213 universal school-based SEL programs involving 270,034 students found significantly improved social-emotional skills, behavior, and academic performance, and a 2024 meta-analysis of 59 studies involving 83,233 participants found an overall effect size of 0.15 with reductions in antisocial behavior and gains in social-emotional outcomes.
edges.population: children and adolescents participating in universal school-based social-emotional learning programs
edges.mechanism: SEL programs build emotional regulation, social problem-solving, empathy, and classroom climate, which can reduce internalizing and behavioral symptoms over time.
edges.summary: School-based social-emotional learning programs consistently improve broad child mental health and behavioral outcomes, though average effects are generally small at the individual level.
edges.caveats: Effects vary by dosage, implementation quality, curriculum design, and baseline student risk. Programs often show broader psychosocial benefits more consistently than disorder-specific symptom remission.
